currentContext.business: The Company operates in the renewable energy sector with a focus on the solar business and allied activities. Its business profile was transformed during FY 2025-26 by the Scheme of Amalgamation of Solar Citizen Private Limited with Citizen Solar Limited (formerly Citizen Infoline Limited), sanctioned by the NCLT Ahmedabad Bench by Order dated March 19, 2026 under Sections 230-232 of the Companies Act, 2013 with an Appointed Date of April 1, 2023; consequently operations are now substantially focused on solar energy. The MD&A describes the sector it addresses as encompassing solar photovoltaic modules and related products, engineering and installation activities, solar power generation and ancillary products and services, serving industrial, commercial and residential consumers; the annual report does not break the Company's own revenue down by any of these sub-activities. The Company is subject to a cost audit (Cost Auditors appointed for FY 2026-27) and employed 66 active employees/members covered under the gratuity valuation as at March 31, 2026.

Solar / renewable energy: Solar business and allied activities (the annual report names no individual product or brand)

currentContext.expansion: The annual report discloses no named capex project, plant, site or commissioning timeline. The only structural expansion event of FY 2025-26 is corporate rather than greenfield: the Scheme of Amalgamation of Solar Citizen Private Limited with Citizen Solar Limited (formerly Citizen Infoline Limited), sanctioned by the NCLT Ahmedabad Bench by Order dated March 19, 2026 under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013 with an Appointed Date of April 1, 2023, after which the Company's operations are 'substantially focused on the solar energy business'. Management describes the amalgamation as having enabled consolidation of business operations, assets, resources, expertise and financial strength under a single corporate structure, expected to provide greater operational and administrative efficiencies and potential economies of scale. Forward expansion intent is stated only qualitatively — strengthening solar operations, expanding the customer and market base, improving capacity utilisation and exploring opportunities in related segments of the renewable-energy value chain — with no capacity addition, location or date attached. Annexure C to the Directors' Report records 'Capital Investment: Nil' under conservation of energy, no technology imported in the last three years and nil R&D expenditure. The Contingent Liabilities and Capital Commitments note states the Company has no capital commitments as at the reporting date.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- MD&A Risks and Threats lists 'changes in government policies, regulations, duties and incentives applicable to the renewable energy sector' first; the solar business depends on a policy-supported demand pool.
- MD&A flags 'volatility in prices and availability of solar modules, cells, components and other raw materials' — input cost is the dominant margin driver for a solar products/EPC business.
- MD&A lists 'dependence on suppliers and supply-chain conditions'; the Board's risk-management note repeats 'supply-chain disruptions'. Strategy also names strengthening supply-chain and vendor relationships as a priority.
- MD&A flags 'technological changes and the risk of technological obsolescence'; solar module efficiency cycles can strand existing product and inventory.
- Named in the MD&A risk list and in the Board's risk-management note as 'competition'.
- MD&A flags 'working capital requirements associated with expansion of operations'; the Board risk note adds 'liquidity and working-capital requirements'. Management also lists disciplined working-capital management as a strategic priority and cites conservation of resources as the reason for its dividend stance.
- MD&A flags 'fluctuations in interest rates and finance costs'; the Company explains the sharp rise in its Debt-Equity Ratio as being 'on account of increase in borrowings during the current year'.
- MD&A lists 'credit risk associated with customers and counterparties'; the Board risk note repeats 'customer credit risk'. The Trade Receivables Turnover Ratio fell 'on account of increase in trade receivables during the current year'.
